title: Self-iterative learning finds RNA-targeting prokaryotic Argonautes and an RNA-modification-sensing activity
summary: The self-iterative hierarchical ensemble model (SIM) nominated six high-confidence prokaryotic Argonaute candidates; five were experimentally validated as RNA-targeting proteins. The study identified three uncharacterized Agos with a novel N-terminal domain, defining a previously unrecognized subclass. Biochemical and in-vivo experiments on Haloferax profundi Ago (HpAgo) established RNA cleavage and a distinctive RNA-modification-sensing capability, which the authors used to build a method for quantifying modified RNA.
ai_technology: Self-Iterative hierarchical ensemble Model (SIM), an ensemble-learning and self-training pipeline
organization: Shanghai Jiao Tong University; ShanghaiTech University and collaborating institutions

evidence.tested: The self-iterative hierarchical ensemble model (SIM) nominated six high-confidence prokaryotic Argonaute candidates; five were experimentally validated as RNA-targeting proteins.
evidence.unknown: Five of six selected candidates were validated; the broader predicted sequence space was not experimentally tested. The specific RNA modification-sensing mechanism and assay performance are supported for HpAgo and tested conditions, not all Argonautes. No therapeutic or universal detection claim is made. Primary abstract/citation record checked; no independent replication assessed.
evidence.ai_role: SIM iteratively expanded its training labels to rank prokaryotic Argonautes for RNA targeting from sparse initial data; it prioritized candidates and identified a previously unrecognized domain-containing subclass. The researchers validated RNA cleavage and RNA-modification sensing biochemically and in vivo.
